title: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate
abstract: arXiv:2610.16426v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated approval systems let coding agents execute high-risk actions with minimal human oversight by delegating the authorization decision to a classifier, typically a large language model (LLM). Such systems, adopted in tools like Claude Code and Codex, remain vulnerable to failure modes such as scope escalation, where the agent takes actions exceeding what the user authorized. Existing benchmarks focus mainly on malicious requests, evaluating refusal under an implicit policy. We introduce AuthGateBench, the first policy-guided benchmark for authorization gating under benign requests. We implement a novel pipeline where an LLM generates contrast pairs with identical action and trajectory but differing request, flipping the label between block and allow. This allows us to assess whether models reason over context rather than the action alone. We further examine whether auxiliary environment signals can help models make better decisions

translated_title: AuthGateBench：将大语言模型作为授权门控的基准测试
translated_abstract: 自动化审批系统通过将授权决策委托给分类器（通常是大语言模型），使编码代理能够在最少人工监督下执行高风险操作。这类系统已被 Claude Code 和 Codex 等工具采用，但仍然容易受到诸如范围升级等失效模式的影响，即代理执行超出用户授权范围的操作。现有基准主要关注恶意请求，在隐式策略下评估拒绝行为。我们提出了 AuthGateBench，这是首个针对良性请求下授权门控的策略引导基准。我们实现了一种新颖的流水线，由大语言模型生成具有相同动作和轨迹但请求不同的对比样本，从而在“阻止”和“允许”标签之间翻转。这使我们能够评估模型是否基于上下文而非仅凭动作本身进行推理。我们进一步研究了辅助环境信号是否能帮助模型做出更好的决策。
tldr: 本文提出首个面向良性请求的策略引导式授权门控基准 AuthGateBench，通过生成动作相同但请求不同的对比样本，评估大语言模型能否结合上下文而不仅是动作本身来做出授权决策。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AuthGateBench, the first policy-guided benchmark for authorization gating under benign requests, which uses contrast pairs with identical actions but differing requests to evaluate whether LLMs reason over context rather than the action alone when making authorization decisions.
